title: Testing Orch OR and Waveguide Models of Consciousness: Anaesthesia, Coherence and the Microtubule
content: Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch OR) identifies consciousness with the collapse of superpositions in microtubules after \(\tau \approx \frac{\hbar}{E_g}\), where \(E_g\) is the self-energy of mass distributions.  We argue this fails under anaesthesia.  Anaesthetics bind hydrophobic pockets in tubulin, abolish consciousness, and leave microtubule mass and mass distribution intact.  Thus \(E_g\) and \(\tau\) remain unchanged while consciousness disappears.  We propose microtubules act as bio-photon waveguides sustaining coherent exciton-photon transport and coupling neurons to \(\mathcal{C}^n\) consciousness field.  Consciousness depends on optical coherence, phase preservation, and waveguide mode integrity, not collapse time.  Anaesthetic binding alters polarizability, dielectric constant, and refractive index, detunes the waveguide, damps dipole oscillations, and destroys coherence.  Washout restores parameters and consciousness.  Orch OR fails because it ties consciousness to \(E_g\), which anaesthesia leaves unchanged; the bio-photon waveguide model succeeds because it ties consciousness to optical coherence, which anaesthesia destroys.
